about.title: Rohnert Park Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Rohnert Park's mix of retail centers, light industrial spaces, and service businesses along corridors like Redwood Drive and Rohnert Park Expressway means workplace injuries here take many forms, from warehouse falls to delivery-related crashes. California generally routes injured workers through the workers' compensation system, which pays medical bills and partial wage replacement regardless of fault, but it doesn't cover everything, and it usually bars a separate lawsuit against your employer. What it doesn't block is a claim against a negligent third party, like a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver, if their carelessness contributed to your injury. Sorting out whether a third party bears responsibility takes a close look at how the injury happened. Our team can review the details of your case and explain what options may be available, at no cost to start.

Burns, chemical exposure, or electrical injuries

whyChoose.title: Why Rohnert Park Workers Choose Us

items.title: We Untangle Workers' Comp From Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still owe you a separate claim. We can help you figure out which path, or both, applies to your situation.

items.title: We Understand the Reporting Clock
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. We review your case quickly so we can help you protect your rights before deadlines slip by.

items.title: We Know Retaliation Is Illegal, and So Should You
items.desc: Employers cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. If you're worried about your job, we can explain your protections and how a third-party claim, which carries its own two-year deadline, fits into the picture.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near Rohnert Park Expressway. Can I sue my employer?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning a separate lawsuit isn't usually available regardless of fault. However, if a third party, like a contractor, equipment supplier, or another driver, contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against them. We can review the specifics and let you know.

items.question: Does workers' comp cover everything if I'm injured on the job in Rohnert Park?
items.answer: Workers' compensation typically covers medical treatment and a portion of lost wages, but it doesn't cover pain and suffering and often falls short of full lost income. That's part of why a third-party claim, when one applies, can matter so much. We can look at your specific losses and explain what's covered and what isn't.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days to preserve your workers' comp rights. If your case involves a third party, that claim carries its own two-year deadline under California law. Because these timelines run separately, it helps to get guidance early rather than waiting.
